facts.display: Public Bank passenger vehicles: up to 90% financing and 108 months for vehicles up to 5 years old; maximum tenures fall to 84, 72 and 60 months for the next published age bands. Vehicles over 10 and up to 12 years old have a published maximum 75% margin and 36-month term. These are maximum limits, subject to assessment.
The Public Bank passenger-vehicle reference supplies financing margins and tenures, not a verified current applicant-specific interest rate. Obtain an actual quotation.
Public Bank home-loan page uses 4.5% as an indicative calculator rate. It is a calculator assumption, not a current personalized loan offer. Approval remains subject to credit evaluation.

Maybank hire purchase publishes financing up to 90% and a term up to 108 months, subject to vehicle and applicant eligibility. The product page describes fixed and variable reducing-balance options effective 1 August 2026.
A verified applicant-specific Maybank car interest rate is not provided in this reference. Compare the actual quotation, rate basis, fees, term and repayment cashflows.

Maybank MaxiHome publishes up to 95% financing including related expenses, with terms up to 35 years or age 70, whichever comes first. The total margin does not imply every borrower receives a 95% asset-only loan.
The reviewed Maybank MaxiHome reference does not establish the applicant's current interest rate. Obtain the bank's quotation and product disclosure sheet.
Maybank personal loan: published amounts RM5,000 to RM100,000, terms 2 to 6 years, Malaysian applicants aged 21 to 60, and minimum gross monthly income RM3,500. Eligibility does not assure approval.

Maybank personal loan advertises fixed headline rates of 8% for RM5,000â€“RM20,000, 7% for RM20,001â€“RM50,000 and 6.5% for RM50,001â€“RM100,000. Confirm calculation basis and effective rate in the actual disclosure; headline rates cannot be directly compared with effective rates.
CIMB hire purchase publishes financing up to 90% and a maximum repayment period of 9 years, subject to product and applicant assessment.

CIMB Islamic car-financing page lists indicative effective profit rates: new national vehicles 6.75%, new foreign 5.10%, unregistered reconditioned 5.65%, used national 8.15% and used foreign 7.40%. These are Islamic indicative references, subject to conditions; confirm the latest quotation with the Auto Finance Centre. They are not conventional flat interest rates.

CIMB HomeFlexi Smart publishes financing up to 95% including MRTA/MLTA, legal and valuation fees, with those extra expenses capped at 5%. The term is up to 35 years or age 70, whichever is earlier. A quoted rate is required.

CIMB Cash Plus publishes RM2,000â€“RM100,000, terms 2â€“7 years, Malaysian applicants aged 21â€“58 with age 60 at maturity, minimum gross monthly income RM2,000, and more than 6 consecutive months of employment. Self-employed business history is more than 24 months.

CIMB Cash Plus advertises fixed rates from 4.38% to 19.88%; 4.38% is for CIMB Preferred and 5.88% for selected CIMB@Work customers, subject to approval. The page gives effective interest rates from 8.08% to 31.42% for its five-year illustrations. A low headline rate is not available to everyone.

Bank Negara Malaysia does not assign a CCRIS credit rating or blacklist borrowers. Its FAQ says rejected loan applications are not provided in CCRIS. Banks use their own credit assessment policies. Do not claim that every rejection automatically damages a CCRIS score.

Internal bank DSR cutoffs, accepted variable income and scoring thresholds are not established by this curated reference. There is no verified universal 60% DSR rule in this knowledge base. Treat any demo affordability threshold as a planning assumption.

BNM's personal-financing policy was issued on 30 September 2025. Specified provisions, including the flat-rate and Rule of 78 restrictions, take effect on 1 January 2027. Do not apply the future provisions as a blanket rule already effective in October 2026.

BNM announced a maximum 70% loan-to-value ratio for a third housing loan when the borrower already has two outstanding housing loan accounts. This is not the same as having owned two properties at any time.
